寤也。从見，學省聲。一曰發也。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kruːɡs, *kruːɡ): phonetic 𦥯 (OC *ɡruːɡ) + semantic 見 (“see”).
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *kruk (“rouse; awaken; disturb”). Cognate with Old Chinese 學 (*ɡruːɡ, “to learn; to study”), 攪 (*kruːʔ, “to disturb”), Tibetan དཀྲུག (dkrug, “to agitate; to rouse”) (Hill, 2012, 2019).

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, 《說文解字》 覺 entry and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry defines 覺 as 寤 (waking), analyzes it as 从見、學省聲, and gives an alternate gloss 發. Duan Yucai argues for 悟 rather than 寤 as the definition, distinguishes 寤 as waking with speech after sleep, and interprets 發 here as alerting someone. This is a historical lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the graph's earliest formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「覺」

evidence.text: The page reports 覺 first attested in Warring States script, with 見 below and a reduced 學 above; it lists Warring States material (睡虎地秦簡《法律答問》10), the Shuowen seal form, and later regular and simplified forms. It explains 見 as seeing/noticing and 學省 as phonetic, while also suggesting a semantic association with learning. Its dating and component analysis are this reference's claims; the page provides no oracle-bone form and no visually inspected glyph evidence in this research.
evidence.title: 覺字形演变字源

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義; historical citations
evidence.text: Records both the large-Xu Shuowen wording 寤也 and Duan's 悟也, each followed by 从見，學省聲，一曰發也. It says the seal form is written with a reduced 學 over 見. Its entry separates senses: waking from sleep, awakening/understanding, noticing or becoming aware, prompting/informing, and sensory perception. It cites 《詩經·王風·兔爰》 尚寐無覺 and 《莊子·齊物論》 覺而後知其夢也 for the wake/awaken sense; further citations include 《荀子·成相》, Tao Yuanming, 《史記》, and 《孟子》 for related senses. These citations establish early textual uses but the page does not date each passage or establish a dated first occurrence for each extension.

gaps: The official Unicode GetUnihanData pages were attempted and failed through the web tool. The requested official click-through evidence could not be verified, so neither local HSK nor secondary Unihan-derived data is offered as external support for current Mandarin readings.

The glyph-history page claims Warring States as the earliest attestation and cites a Qin slip, but the specific glyph image and inscription were not independently inspected; the source reports no oracle-bone forms. A secure earliest extant graphic form therefore remains unverified here.

The reduced upper 學 component is supported by the Shuowen analysis and the glyph-history reference. The evidence supports a phonetic role; the asserted additional semantic contribution of 學 as 'learning' is not established independently and should remain a secondary interpretation.

No independently checked Baxter–Sagart rows for 覺 and 學 were available. The listed Wiktionary reconstructions are in a distinct source presentation; a precise system-to-system sound comparison is therefore unresolved.

The sources consulted establish several early semantic uses but do not provide dated first attestations for all senses or a fully documented chain linking waking, awareness, prompting, and sleep as separate lexical developments. No whole-graph phonetic-loan claim is evidenced in this dossier; the proposed 學 element is a component inside 覺, so uncertainty about 學's own graphic origin does not itself negate its proposed sound role.

The earliest dated graphic evidence available through inspected references is reported Qin slip material; no oracle-bone or bronze 覺 form was supported by the opened references. The ZDIC page reports slip examples but does not itself establish the artifact’s absolute date or show an inspected artifact photograph.

The current official Unicode Unihan per-character pages could not be accessed, so current kMandarin for 觉, 覺, or 學 is not asserted. Secondary reading pages list Mandarin readings, but these are not substituted for official Unihan records.

The local dossier states that the full Unihan_Readings.txt and baxtersagart.tsv sources are absent and the HSK extract does not cover these characters. External Baxter–Sagart dataset inspection supports 覺 rows; 學 reading was found through a secondary page, not an exact local row or verified author-dataset page content.

The dictionary examples establish old textual uses but not securely dated first occurrences for each separate sense. No chronology is inferred from the order of dictionary glosses; relations from physical waking to awareness, prompting, or the later jiào ‘sleep’ reading are not fully demonstrated by these references.

Shuowen gives 見 as the semantic component and reduced 學 as phonetic. A secondary traditional account links waking with awareness/seeing, but independent evidence that 見 contributes the meaning is limited; the alternative claim that 學 also contributes ‘learning’ semantically is not established. No whole-graph loan is evidenced.

The tested Qin-slip image is an educational modern vector redraw sourced to Xiaoxuetang’s Qin slip label 睡·法10. It is not an ancient artifact photo. No Xiaoxuetang query form was supplied in this invocation; the image is proposed through its Commons provenance page and direct file URL.

The repository dossier says the full local Unihan readings file and Baxter–Sagart TSV are absent; its HSK extract does not cover 覺 or 觉. The official Unicode per-character records also failed during this invocation, so no kMandarin value or official Unihan character record is asserted. The dictionary’s Mandarin readings are used only as dictionary evidence.

The inspected sources report Qin-slip material labeled 睡·法10 as an early graphic form, but the inscription itself was not independently inspected and no secure artifact date was verified here. The Xiaoxuetang request for 覺 returned HTTP 401 in the supplied invocation; that candidate and query are unavailable for this run.

The Shuowen and MOE records support 學省 as a phonetic component and 見 as the traditional analysis’s semantic component. A further semantic contribution from 學 (‘learning’) appears in Guoxuedashi but is not independently established. No whole-graph phonetic-loan claim is evidenced; the sound analysis concerns 學省 within 覺.

Dictionary citations attest waking in the 《詩經》 and 《莊子》 texts and later listed uses for understanding, awareness/discovery, prompting, and perception, but they do not date each individual occurrence. The semantic links and chronology among these senses remain unproven here. The later jiào ‘sleep’ sense is separately listed; its development is not established by these sources.

The Commons seal-script file is a modern vector redraw of a reported historical style, not an artifact photo. Its description page supports identity and reuse rights, but the resolved direct image URL returned a cache-miss error when opened in this invocation, so no glyph is proposed for download. The Qin-slip candidate was previously reported as HTTP 404 and was not retried.
No official Unicode Unihan record was searched or opened in this verification task. Current MOE readings are distinct from Baxter–Sagart reconstructions; no reconstruction claim is made here.

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons 覺 seal.svg 覺篆書 file; Baxter Sagart 覺 and 學 readings
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Commons file provenance and official Baxter–Sagart tables. The table gives 學 *m-kˤruk and 覺 *kˤruk in the same system; the alternate 覺 reading jiào is not used to characterize the jué comparison.

search_audit.query: Unicode official GetUnihanData records for U+89C9, U+89BA, and U+5B78
search_audit.outcome: Attempted all three official individual records; each returned Internal Error. Opened UAX #38, which documents kMandarin as a Unihan property.

gaps: The repository dossier says the full local Unihan readings file and Baxter–Sagart TSV are absent; its HSK extract does not cover 覺 or 觉. The official Unicode per-character records also failed during this invocation, so no kMandarin value or official Unihan character record is asserted. The dictionary’s Mandarin readings are used only as dictionary evidence.

The inspected sources report Qin-slip material labeled 睡·法10 as an early graphic form, but the inscription itself was not independently inspected and no secure artifact date was verified here. The Xiaoxuetang request for 覺 returned HTTP 401 in the supplied invocation; that candidate and query are unavailable for this run.

The Shuowen and MOE records support 學省 as a phonetic component and 見 as the traditional analysis’s semantic component. A further semantic contribution from 學 (‘learning’) appears in Guoxuedashi but is not independently established. No whole-graph phonetic-loan claim is evidenced; the sound analysis concerns 學省 within 覺.

Dictionary citations attest waking in the 《詩經》 and 《莊子》 texts and later listed uses for understanding, awareness/discovery, prompting, and perception, but they do not date each individual occurrence. The semantic links and chronology among these senses remain unproven here. The later jiào ‘sleep’ sense is separately listed; its development is not established by these sources.

The Commons seal-script file is a modern vector redraw of a reported historical style, not an artifact photo. Its description page supports identity and reuse rights, but the resolved direct image URL returned a cache-miss error when opened in this invocation, so no glyph is proposed for download. The Qin-slip candidate was previously reported as HTTP 404 and was not retried.
